text:
Rina Kapoor: dropping a quick note after the review  regarding form validation and delete flows. Short thread.
Jon Park: quick take: field-level inline errors for input-specific problems; a small, dismissible top banner for submit/server errors.
Diego Morales: inline errors should be short and not push layout. Use fade-in and keep single-line copy.
Priya Singh: agree. For required fields: asterisk + a small legend at the top that says '* = required'. Also add sr-only text on labels.
Rina Kapoor: on destructive actions: delete workspace/button currently in header. Should we move it to the bottom or keep header but low prominence?
Jon Park: keep it discoverable in header for power users but make it outline style and require explicit confirm to avoid accidents.
Diego Morales: typed-confirm is our safest bet. Could be inline (expand under button) instead of a modal. Inline helps maintain context.
Priya Singh: inline is good, but make sure to announce expansion to screen readers and provide `aria-describedby` on the confirm input explaining permanence.
Rina Kapoor: fallback modal for mobile?
Jon Park: yes — inline for desktop, modal for small viewports (<420px). Keep copy identical between both.
Diego Morales: sample markup suggestion: `<input aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="name-error" />` and error node `role="alert"`.
Priya Singh: add `aria-live` on the inline confirm container so SRs get notified when it opens. Also ensure focus moves into the confirm input.
DesignBot: accessibility scan: missing `aria-invalid` on current prototypes, flagging color contrast on error text (aim for 4.5:1), recommend `role=alert` on revealed errors.
Rina Kapoor: thanks. Action items: Rina to update mock with inline errors + banner; Diego to prototype inline typed-confirm with mobile modal fallback; Jon to add e2e SR tests. Will reconvene after mocks posted. :thumbsup:
